court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Aditya Anand Varma And Ors vs The State Of Maharashtra And Anr

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Aditya Anand Varma, Anand Prakash Varma, Aarti Anand Varma (husband, wife, and child)
parties.respondent_defendant: The State of Maharashtra, Harsha Aditya Varma (nee) Harsha Singh (complainant in domestic violence application)

acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Petitioners sought to challenge an order rejecting their domestic violence application. Respondent No.2 filed a complaint under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005. The trial court rejected the petition.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking extraordinary writ jurisdiction to demonstrate that the statutory remedy is inadequate.
legal_principles.held: It would be hazardous to rely upon the said order as a precedent, since it simply lacks the precedential value.
applicable_acts_sections: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005 — Section 29
cited_cases: Parvez Kapadia and Ors. V/s. Pravin P. Kapadia and Anr., (2022) X SCC Y
Siddharth Sabharwal V/s. State of Maharashtra, (2019) SCC Online Bom 3106

legal_principles.principle: The court will not entertain a petition under extraordinary writ jurisdiction if the statutory remedy is available and has not been exhausted.
legal_principles.held: Therefore, it was possible for the Petitioner to file the appeal instead of filing the present Petition.
applicable_acts_sections: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005 — Section 29
cited_cases: Siddharth Sabharwal V/s. State of Maharashtra, (2019) SCC Online Bom 3106

outcome.final_order: The final order was that the writ petition is dismissed.
